description: The last stage of detector postprocessing, and the one with no fixture until now: boxes leave NMS in letterboxed network pixels and must arrive as NormalizedBox in oriented-image coordinates before they mean anything to anyone.

rules.boxes_are_clipped: A NormalizedBox is a location in the image, so it is clipped to [0,1]. A box claiming to extend past the frame is not describing anything a renderer can crop.
rules.landmarks_are_not_clipped: Point2D bounds are deliberately loose ([-0.5, 1.5]). A face clipped by the frame edge genuinely has an eye off-frame, and clamping it onto the border would move the alignment template and produce a subtly wrong warp -- confidently wrong rather than absent, the worst failure mode here.
rules.empty_intersection_is_dropped: A detection with no overlap with the oriented image is not a detection. It cannot be clipped into a valid NormalizedBox (w and h are exclusiveMinimum 0), so it must be dropped rather than emitted degenerate.

cases.name: entirely above the image, inside the letterbox padding

note: The padding band is not empty to a detector: it is uniform grey, and a detector will occasionally fire on it. The third case is what that looks like. A host that clamps instead of dropping emits a zero-height box at y=0, which passes as a face at the top edge of every affected photo.
